notice: Source index only. WP-04 expands these broad rows into reviewed atomic inventory, not a completed content bank.

rows.description: Recognize selected Spanish letters/marks and enter a reviewed short written form with the normal keyboard.
sourceCells: S4 sections 1.1-1.3; device operation is a product prerequisite, not a CEFR claim.

rows.description: Notice and preserve written accents in familiar reviewed words, with initial stress awareness.
sourceCells: S4 sections 2.1-2.2; fuller distinctions return with relevant vocabulary/grammar.

rows.description: Use opening/closing question/exclamation marks, sentence punctuation, and basic capitalization in a supported short phrase.
sourceCells: S4 sections 1.4-1.5 and 3.1/3.6; not all orthography is taught in this block.

rows.description: Follow an exercise instruction and consult an inline explanation of a needed grammar term.
sourceCells: Original support objective; introduce terms in context, without a separate terminology exam.

rows.description: Letters and written marks: accented vowels, ñ, ü, ¿ and ¡; ordinary computer/phone entry.
sourceCells: Recognize a written form, enter a familiar short word, and correct a supplied form. C-056 excludes an on-screen character strip. Revisit the same writing target in later vocabulary.

rows.description: Initial stress awareness and written accents through a small reviewed word set.
sourceCells: Identify/preserve a mark, repair a supported word, and later recall it with its meaning/context. Contrast examples must not silently test unintroduced grammar. C-077 assigns an initial reviewed fixed-phrase listening component; recognition and writing evidence remain separate.

rows.description: A short written phrase: punctuation, opening/closing signs, capitalization, and exercise-instruction help.
sourceCells: Restore punctuation and write a brief familiar phrase. Explain noun/verb/person or other terms only when the task needs them. Return to the target in later questions and messages. Include the reviewed everyday fixed-phrase/listening starter (CV-01).

rows.description: Short optional checkpoint and a later independent return.
sourceCells: Sample the introduced writing targets without a visible answer model; keep help available, attribute it to the actual target, and retain uncertain results. No mandatory perfect score or new topic lock.

rows.description: Recall a familiar noun with an appropriate article/gender pairing, including selected common exceptions rather than inferring every gender from an ending.
sourceCells: S1 section 1, noun gender; exact subitems to reconcile.

rows.description: Select definite/indefinite articles in a short context that makes the intended reference sufficiently clear.
sourceCells: S1 section 3, articles.

rows.description: Produce singular/plural noun phrases with matching article and number.
sourceCells: S1 section 1, noun number, and section 3.

rows.description: Add a familiar qualifying adjective with appropriate gender/number agreement in an introduced pattern.
sourceCells: S1 sections 2.1-2.3.

rows.description: Express simple possession using reviewed possessives and context that resolves the intended possessor.
sourceCells: S1 section 5; form/meaning distinctions need full mapping.

rows.description: A noun with its article: learn a reviewed noun/article pair and selected common gender patterns/exceptions.
sourceCells: Recognize, complete, then recall a short familiar expression. Separate unknown-word help from a demonstrated agreement error.

rows.description: Definite and indefinite articles in introduced contexts.
sourceCells: Choose an article, explain the context in Ukrainian when needed, and write the short phrase. Accept alternatives if the context supports them; avoid an arbitrary single-key verdict.

rows.description: Singular and plural, changing the noun phrase together.
sourceCells: Transform, correct agreement, and write a familiar singular/plural phrase. Later combine number with adjectives and possession.

rows.description: Describing people/objects with familiar adjectives.
sourceCells: Choose/produce agreement and build a short noun phrase. Broader placement differences and unintroduced vocabulary remain for later mapped lessons. Stage basic degree wording in small supporting steps (CV-02).

rows.description: Possession: my, your, and other introduced possessors.
sourceCells: Begin with a small set of forms, then expand to other A1 inventory forms including Spain-relevant plural-possessor forms with supporting context. Do not demand pronoun/conjugation knowledge not yet introduced. Teach needed possession/preposition frames at first use (CV-03).

rows.description: Optional mixed check and delayed independent return.
sourceCells: Combine article, noun, number, adjective, and possession only where introduced. Keep help available; record separate target evidence rather than a single whole-block pass/fail.

rows.description: Build an introduced short sentence and connect its subject/person to the verb form.
sourceCells: Introduce common patterns and pronouns gradually; accept reviewed natural subject omission where appropriate.

rows.description: Express basic identity, origin, or an introduced description with ser.
sourceCells: Contextual meaning and permitted wording need review; do not replace use distinctions with an unqualified permanent/temporary slogan.

rows.description: Express a known referent's location or an introduced state with estar.
sourceCells: Limit the first adjective/state set to reviewed uses; broader contrasts return later.

rows.description: Say that something is present using an introduced hay frame and distinguish it from locating a specified referent.
sourceCells: Supply sufficient context and avoid silent tests of untaught determiner/preposition patterns.

rows.description: Express possession or a small set of introduced tener meanings.
sourceCells: Age expressions may be included only with already introduced numbers; broader number work remains A1-05.

rows.description: Ask a short introduced question and produce a negative sentence.
sourceCells: Begin with accessible written patterns; detailed question-word coverage continues in A1-05.

rows.description: The short sentence: subject/person, an introduced verb pattern, and useful word order.
sourceCells: Build a sentence from familiar elements, complete a form, and write a short statement. Provide person/pronoun reference on demand. Teach introduced pronoun/article/possessive accent contrasts (CV-03).

rows.description: Ser for introduced identity/origin/description contexts.
sourceCells: Form practice and short meaning-to-sentence tasks. Reuse article/adjective targets selectively; record the actual target of any help. Add supported introductions and a synthetic identity/form context with taught labels (CV-01/CV-06).

rows.description: Estar for location and a small reviewed state set.
sourceCells: Match context and sentence, complete the form, and describe a familiar location/state. Contrast with already introduced ser only when meaning is clear. Introduce the needed location/preposition frames before assessment (CV-03).

rows.description: Hay and estar: what is there versus where a known thing/person is.
sourceCells: Use a short authored situation, contextual choice, and short production; do not force a unique verdict when both readings are supported.

rows.description: Tener: possession and useful introduced expressions.
sourceCells: Write about a familiar possession; add other meanings only with supporting vocabulary already taught. Revisit A1-02 possession from a sentence perspective.

rows.description: Questions and negative sentences with these patterns.
sourceCells: Turn an introduced statement into a question/negative, understand the written question, and give a short written answer. No spoken response is required.

rows.description: Optional mixed check and delayed independent return.
sourceCells: Mix introduced patterns with adequate context. Keep verb form, contextual selection, agreement, and any listening evidence distinct.

rows.description: Produce introduced regular -ar present forms in a familiar action sentence.
sourceCells: Connect infinitive, person, and ending; exact paradigms and lexical set require review.

rows.description: Produce introduced regular -er present forms.
sourceCells: Distinguish a form task from independently choosing a meaningful action.

rows.description: Produce introduced regular -ir present forms and distinguish the taught -er/-ir endings.
sourceCells: Teach the two patterns in small steps; use familiar verbs and reviewed person contrasts.

rows.description: Recall a limited set of useful irregular present forms, initially proposed for ir and hacer, while revisiting previously introduced forms.
sourceCells: Each assessed exception remains identifiable for review. The exact set is pending; broader vowel/consonant changes and their systematization return in A2-01.

rows.description: Use an introduced daily-routine pronominal pattern with person-appropriate pronoun and verb form.
sourceCells: Start with a small reviewed set, such as a levantarse pattern. Separate pronoun/person selection from conjugation; this does not teach the complete object-pronoun system.

rows.description: Express basic frequency in a reviewed routine frame.
sourceCells: Introduce the meaning/placement of each expression first. Detailed clock time, dates, and number work remain A1-05; a broad adverb inventory is not assumed.

rows.description: Read a short routine and write a brief description or written answer using introduced material.
sourceCells: Reuse questions/negation from A1-03. Provide any needed connector/time expression before assessing it; broader linking and messages continue in A1-06.

rows.description: Regular -ar action verbs, connecting the person to the present form (O1).
sourceCells: Complete a form, change an introduced person, then write a familiar action sentence. Keep the infinitive/person reference available as recorded help.

rows.description: Regular -er and -ir in two short steps, then a focused comparison (O2/O3).
sourceCells: Practice each family separately before mixing them. Attribute an ending error to the relevant family/person rather than the whole present tense.

rows.description: A small useful irregular-form set, initially proposed for ir and hacer (O4).
sourceCells: Recall a specific form, use it in a familiar context, and revisit earlier ser/estar/tener forms selectively. Do not introduce a full irregular-verb catalog at once. Teach needed destination/contraction frames with introduced ir (CV-03).

rows.description: Daily-routine expressions with an introduced pronominal pattern (O5).
sourceCells: Select the person/pronoun, produce the form, and write a short routine action. Assess pronoun selection and verb formation separately where the prompt supports that distinction.

rows.description: How often: everyday frequency expressions in familiar sentences (O6).
sourceCells: Match meaning, place a reviewed expression, and write a true-to-prompt routine sentence. Exact expression choices and placement variants require review.

rows.description: Put the day together: a short text and brief written routine (O7).
sourceCells: Read for meaning, answer a familiar question, and write a few connected statements using only introduced patterns. No live conversation or spoken response. Stage the adopted sequence-link support before integrated writing (CV-04).

rows.description: Optional mixed check and delayed independent return.
sourceCells: Sample the introduced regular families, selected exceptions, pronominal pattern, and frequency. Preserve specific target evidence; no single whole-tense pass/fail or mandatory perfect score.

rows.description: Recognize and produce introduced number/quantity expressions in a familiar context.
sourceCells: S1 section 6.1 supplies numeral/quantifier families. Specify manageable cardinal ranges, a useful ordinal subset, and agreement patterns during authoring; do not silently test an untaught larger number.

rows.description: Understand a familiar price and ask/answer about the amount.
sourceCells: Teach currency and amount wording with reviewed variants. Arithmetic is not a language target; broader shopping requests continue elsewhere.

rows.description: Understand a clock time or short opening-hours entry and distinguish asking the current time from asking when an event starts.
sourceCells: S5 section 4.1 supplies partial time/hour references. Teach the necessary time/preposition frames; specify accepted numeric/written representations for each task.

rows.description: Understand and express introduced days, dates, and a simple appointment reference.
sourceCells: S5 provides partial temporal anchors only. Review exact day/month/date forms and context; resolve ambiguous numeric dates explicitly.

rows.description: Locate a known place/object or ask where it is using introduced spatial expressions.
sourceCells: Revisit hay/estar with familiar nouns and a small taught spatial set. Exact preposition coverage is pending; full route instructions/imperatives remain A2-07.

rows.description: Select an introduced question pattern for the information actually missing and write a short question.
sourceCells: S1 sections 7.3 and 8.8 supply partial interrogative anchors. Meaning, agreement, accents, and person/form remain distinguishable targets; exact question-word coverage needs reconciliation.

rows.description: Extract relevant details from a short practical text and give a written answer or clarification question.
sourceCells: Use introduced grammar and familiar words. Finding information in text is distinct from producing a Spanish number/question form; broader messages continue in A1-06.

rows.description: Numbers and quantities in small practical steps (O1).
sourceCells: Match an amount, write an introduced number form, and build a reviewed quantity phrase. Add a small practical ordinal set only after explaining it; keep individual patterns available for focused review. Receive age-after-numbers and targeted quantity contrasts (CV-02/CV-04).

rows.description: Prices and amounts (O2).
sourceCells: Read a synthetic price label, understand the amount, and ask/answer a familiar price question. Separate numeric comprehension from required Spanish wording. Add reviewed shop/service formulas and their listening targets (CV-01/CV-06).

rows.description: Clock time and opening hours (O3).
sourceCells: Read a short schedule, distinguish current/event time, and give a suitable question or answer. Teach introduced expressions/prepositions before independent checks.

rows.description: Days, dates, and a simple appointment (O4).
sourceCells: Find a day/date, complete a reviewed calendar expression, and write a short appointment question/answer with explicit context.

rows.description: Where something is: places and basic spatial expressions (O5).
sourceCells: Use a short written scene or accessible simple plan with text support. Ask/answer about location and revisit hay/estar only when context supports the distinction. Stage the selected spatial frames and contractions (CV-03).

rows.description: Ask for the missing information (O6/O7).
sourceCells: Read a short notice, identify what is known/missing, choose a question pattern, and write a brief question or answer. Accept reviewed equivalent questions when they request the same needed information.

rows.description: Optional mixed check and delayed independent return.
sourceCells: Combine familiar prices, hours, dates, locations, and questions in a short practical situation. Sample specific targets rather than awarding one whole-block mastery label.

rows.description: Express a familiar like/dislike using an introduced gustar pattern.
sourceCells: S6 section 3.2 and S1 section 15.1.1 supply partial anchors. Begin with a small pronoun/reference set; distinguish experiencer selection, gusta/gustan agreement, and noun/infinitive framing. Broader pronoun coverage returns in A2-02.

rows.description: Express a choice between familiar options using introduced preference wording.
sourceCells: S6 sections 3.4-3.5 supply anchors. Teach the selected preferir forms first and review individual exceptions; broader comparisons remain A2-02.

rows.description: Express a practical need with an introduced necesitar plus noun/infinitive frame.
sourceCells: A proposed realization of the accepted needs outcome, requiring full source/variant review. Keep need distinct from liking or wanting. Broader ability, permission, and obligation patterns require explicit placement in A2-01/A2-07 during coverage reconciliation.

rows.description: Express a simple wish with an introduced querer plus noun/infinitive frame.
sourceCells: S6 section 3.8 and S1 section 15.1.1 supply partial anchors. Teach selected irregular forms and the infinitive construction; do not treat a wish alone as evidence of a definite plan.

rows.description: Express an introduced simple plan with a present form and an explicit future time context.
sourceCells: S6 sections 3.9-3.10 supply partial anchors. Reuse reviewed present/time vocabulary; ir a plus infinitive and broader time contrasts are developed in A2-01.

rows.description: Join familiar ideas using a small taught set of addition, contrast, and reason patterns.
sourceCells: S1 section 14 supplies partial coordination anchors; the proposed starter set is y, pero, porque. The reason pattern's exact source mapping and alternatives need review; this is not the complete connector inventory.

rows.description: Extract the relevant meaning from a short personal message and identify a suitable response.
sourceCells: Use introduced language and sufficient context. Text comprehension is separate from independently producing the same construction.

rows.description: Write a short message that fulfills a familiar practical intent.
sourceCells: Use introduced patterns and reviewed valid variants. A suggested few-sentence length is guidance, not a hard word-count or CEFR certification threshold.

rows.description: Likes and dislikes with a small gustar pattern set (O1).
sourceCells: Match intended meaning, complete the relevant pronoun/form, then write a short familiar statement. Separate help with the experiencer, agreement, and vocabulary. Include selected short responses and reviewed gustar-family extensions in small supporting steps (CV-02/CV-05).

rows.description: Express a preference between familiar options (O2).
sourceCells: Introduce selected preferir wording/forms, choose a suitable response, and produce a short preference sentence. Do not silently require a new comparison structure.

rows.description: What is needed: necesitar with a familiar thing or action (O3).
sourceCells: Distinguish the meaning of a need, build the introduced noun/infinitive frame, and write a useful short statement or answer.

rows.description: Wishes and simple plans in two small steps (O4/O5).
sourceCells: Introduce querer plus noun/infinitive, then a reviewed present-plus-time plan. Practice their meanings separately before mixing them; broader future constructions return in A2-01.

rows.description: Connect ideas with y, pero, and porque (O6).
sourceCells: Recognize the intended relationship, choose a reviewed connector, and join familiar clauses. Preserve valid alternatives when context supports them; exact punctuation/variant rules need review. Receive the adopted response/sequence-link support (CV-02/CV-04).

rows.description: A short personal message: understand and write a useful response (O7/O8).
sourceCells: Read a small prepared message, identify its practical intent, and write a few relevant sentences using introduced preferences, needs, wishes/plans, and links. Provide a small reviewed opening/closing where needed.

rows.description: Optional cumulative A1 check and delayed independent return.
sourceCells: Sample introduced targets from A1-01 through A1-06 using familiar contexts, short text/audio comprehension, and written production. Offer small resumable parts and specific follow-up practice. It is not an overall proficiency certificate or a mandatory perfect-score lock for A2.

rows.description: Produce introduced frequent present stem-change patterns for the intended person.
sourceCells: S1 section 9.1.1 is the present-family anchor. Select a manageable verb/person set and review the exact contrasts; do not generalize one verb's behavior to every person or verb.

rows.description: Recall selected other irregular or spelling-dependent present forms in familiar sentences.
sourceCells: S1 section 9.1.1; individual forms/patterns remain identifiable for focused review. Revisit prior exceptions instead of resetting the whole present tense.

rows.description: Form a reviewed gerund from an introduced verb, including a small selected exception set.
sourceCells: S1 section 9.4.2 supplies the gerund anchor. Keep regular formation and individual exceptions distinguishable; exact lexical set requires review.

rows.description: Build an introduced estar plus gerund sentence with the appropriate auxiliary/person form.
sourceCells: S1 sections 9.4.2 and 12.1. Track auxiliary production separately from gerund formation. Broader pronoun placement is developed in A2-02; use supported basic patterns here.

rows.description: Choose a reviewed present/simple-progressive formulation that suits a sufficiently clear context.
sourceCells: Require reviewed meaning/variants; a time word alone is not an infallible construction selector. If both formulations are natural for the supplied meaning, accept reviewed alternatives or clarify the task.

rows.description: Express an introduced plan/intention using ir a plus infinitive and a clear time context.
sourceCells: S1 section 12.1 and S6 sections 3.9-3.10 supply partial anchors. Distinguish the taught action-plan frame from familiar movement/location wording; broader future morphology is not implied.

rows.description: Express an introduced ability/possibility meaning with poder plus infinitive.
sourceCells: S1 section 12.1 supplies the modal-family anchor. Select and explain the intended meaning; permission/request applications continue in A2-07.

rows.description: Express a personal obligation with an introduced tener que plus infinitive pattern.
sourceCells: S1 section 12.1; distinguish the intended obligation from a wish/plan. Broader impersonal obligation and practical instructions continue in A2-07.

rows.description: Read a short familiar situation and write an appropriate account or response using introduced constructions.
sourceCells: Keep reading comprehension, form production, and contextual construction choice distinguishable. Use reviewed variants rather than a single required message wording.

rows.description: Frequent present stem changes in manageable reviewed steps (O1).
sourceCells: Compare introduced person/forms, complete a targeted form, and use it in a familiar sentence. Keep a specific pattern/form available for direct practice.

rows.description: Other selected irregular and spelling-dependent present forms (O2).
sourceCells: Recall specific forms, correct a supported example, and write a short sentence. Exact first-person and other pattern allocation remains authoring work.

rows.description: Gerund formation: regular patterns and a small exception set (O3).
sourceCells: Form the introduced non-finite form, recognize a relevant exception, and revisit it independently later. This checks form production before assuming contextual selection.

rows.description: An action in progress: estar plus gerund, then contextual use (O4/O5).
sourceCells: Build the sentence, select an appropriate formulation, and describe a familiar ongoing situation. Review acceptable overlaps with simple present before grading choices.

rows.description: Plans/intention with ir a plus infinitive (O6).
sourceCells: Form the pattern, understand a short plan, and write one with explicit time context. Revisit A1-06 wishes/present-plus-time plans with enough meaning context.

rows.description: Ability and obligation in two small steps: poder / tener que plus infinitive (O7/O8).
sourceCells: Teach each frame and its selected meaning before mixing them. Track verb forms, infinitive framing, and ability/obligation meaning separately. Place the adopted supporting infinitive-construction steps after this foundation; review size before authoring (CV-05).

rows.description: Put the situation together: routine, current action, and plan (O9).
sourceCells: Read a short situation and write a relevant description or response, adding ability/obligation only where introduced and needed. Explain why a construction fits while preserving valid alternatives. Receive familiar present weather/state frames before later past descriptions (CV-04).

rows.description: Optional mixed check and delayed independent return.
sourceCells: Sample introduced present forms, gerund/auxiliary production, and contextual meanings using familiar material. Keep it resumable and retain specific review targets instead of a whole-block mastery label.

rows.description: Identify and use an introduced demonstrative reference with a clear antecedent/context.
sourceCells: Section 4; introduce or refresh the necessary forms explicitly rather than assuming an earlier block taught every demonstrative.

rows.description: Express introduced possession without repeating the possessed noun.
sourceCells: Section 5, tonic possessive forms; review agreement and permitted article/standalone patterns.

rows.description: Refer to a familiar direct object using an introduced unstressed pronoun.
sourceCells: Section 7.1.2; distinguish object role, intended referent, and gender/number/person selection.

rows.description: Refer to a familiar recipient/indirect object using an introduced pronoun pattern.
sourceCells: Sections 7.1.3 and 7.1.6; introduce needed tonic/prepositional support in small steps. Keep gustar-type experiencer and recipient tasks distinguishable.

rows.description: Place an introduced pronoun in reviewed finite, infinitive, and gerund frames.
sourceCells: Sections 7.1.2-7.1.3 with prior A2-01 frames. Review valid placement alternatives; imperative placement follows its introduction in A2-07.

rows.description: Use a small reviewed set of two-pronoun combinations.
sourceCells: Section 7.1.3 includes the le/les-to-se pattern before a direct-object pronoun. Track role/form, order, and replacement separately; this does not cover every use of se.

rows.description: Compare introduced qualities/quantities using a reviewed regular comparison frame.
sourceCells: Sections 2.5, 6.1, and 15.3.8; stage inequality/equality and agreement patterns rather than testing all at once.

rows.description: Recall selected frequent irregular comparison forms in an appropriate meaning context.
sourceCells: Section 2.5; exact forms/uses and permissible alternatives require review. A form task does not prove independent comparison choice.

rows.description: Add a useful detail to a familiar description with introduced adjective/sentence patterns and a simple relative que frame.
sourceCells: Sections 7.2 and 15.2; teach the new frame, reuse reviewed agreement/ser/estar, and retain introduced present-time contexts.

rows.description: Read a short description/comparison and write a relevant description, choice, or response.
sourceCells: Original integrated objective using the introduced reference/comparison targets. Reading, contextual selection, and written production remain distinguishable evidence.

rows.description: Refer without repeating a noun: demonstratives and possessive references in two short steps (O1/O2).
sourceCells: Identify the referent, choose a reviewed form, and write a short reference. Keep the two pattern families separate in evidence.

rows.description: Replace a direct object with an introduced pronoun (O3).
sourceCells: Link a familiar noun to the pronoun, choose its form, and produce a short sentence with explicit context.

rows.description: Refer to the recipient/indirect object (O4).
sourceCells: Identify who receives/is affected in the introduced frame, select the pronoun, and write the short statement. Explain any needed prepositional/tonic form first. Teach needed tonic/prepositional and meaningful accent distinctions before assessment (CV-03).

rows.description: Where the pronoun goes (O5).
sourceCells: Use the already introduced present, infinitive, and gerund constructions. Practice reviewed placement variants without marking one valid alternative wrong.

rows.description: Combine two pronouns in a small familiar pattern set (O6).
sourceCells: Begin with explicit referents, then practice form/order and the introduced se replacement separately. Revisit the actual difficult component later.

rows.description: Compare familiar options: regular frames, then selected frequent exceptions (O7/O8).
sourceCells: Compare a quality or quantity, complete the introduced frame, and write a suitable comparison. Teach each pattern/exception before mixing them.

rows.description: Add a detail to a description (O9).
sourceCells: Reuse familiar adjectives/agreement and introduced ser/estar meanings; teach a simple relative que construction before short independent descriptions. Connect the introduced relative/question accent contrast (CV-03).

rows.description: Read, compare, and describe a familiar choice (O10).
sourceCells: Use synthetic product/home/person descriptions with familiar words; give a short written choice or description using introduced patterns. Introduce the adopted negative/reference patterns before using them independently here (CV-02).

rows.description: Optional mixed check and delayed independent return.
sourceCells: Sample introduced reference, placement, comparison, and description targets in short resumable parts. Retain specific evidence instead of a single whole-block mastery label.

rows.description: Produce the appropriate present haber auxiliary for the intended person.
sourceCells: S1 9.1.6 and S7 model 36; teach the compound-tense role explicitly rather than reusing impersonal hay as the answer model. Include Spain-relevant plural forms.

rows.description: Form a regular participle from an introduced infinitive.
sourceCells: S1 9.1.6 and S7 regular models; teach -ar/-ado and -er/-ir/-ido formation with a reviewed lexical set.

rows.description: Recall individual introduced irregular participles.
sourceCells: Initial proposed examples: hecho, dicho, escrito, visto, supported by S1/S7. Specify/review the final set; keep each difficult form identifiable for later practice.

rows.description: Preserve relevant written accents in introduced participles.
sourceCells: S7 model 40 records leído. Teach the needed writing/stress pattern before assessment; exact additional forms and orthographic mapping remain pending.

rows.description: Build introduced statements, questions, and negatives with the appropriate word/pronoun placement.
sourceCells: Reuse prior sentence and pronoun work. Teach an initial canonical frame, then review valid variants; do not invent an absolute ban on every item between auxiliary and participle.

rows.description: Keep the participle in the reviewed invariant form with auxiliary haber.
sourceCells: S8 28.5a supplies the compound-tense agreement boundary. Explain any contrast with an already introduced adjective/state use only as needed; do not silently test new passive grammar.

rows.description: Select an appropriate introduced perfecto meaning in sufficient context.
sourceCells: S1 9.1.6 anchors past relevance to the present with explicit/implicit temporal framing. Review Spain usage and permissible alternatives; a marker alone is not a universal answer rule.

rows.description: Extract the meaning of a short familiar account using the introduced tense.
sourceCells: Distinguish reading/listening comprehension from recalling the auxiliary/participle in writing. Teach needed time/adverb vocabulary first.

rows.description: Write a brief relevant account or answer using introduced forms and context.
sourceCells: Review accepted variants rather than requiring one reference wording. Broader past contrasts follow the relevant introductions in A2-04 through A2-06.

rows.description: The compound pattern and present haber auxiliary (O1).
sourceCells: Understand a supported model, connect person to the auxiliary, and complete a short familiar sentence. Record auxiliary help separately from participle help.

rows.description: Regular participles with -ado/-ido (O2).
sourceCells: Form the participle, add it to a familiar sentence, and later recall it in a different reviewed context.

rows.description: A manageable set of irregular participles (O3).
sourceCells: Introduce and practice selected forms such as hecho/dicho/escrito/visto individually before mixing them. A difficulty with one form does not reset every exception or the whole tense.

rows.description: Written accents in familiar participles (O4).
sourceCells: Start with a reviewed form such as leído, explain the needed mark, and revisit spelling separately from auxiliary or contextual meaning.

rows.description: Put the sentence together: questions, negatives, pronouns, and invariant participle (O5/O6).
sourceCells: Reuse already introduced patterns, teach the compound-specific placement/agreement boundary, and accept reviewed natural alternatives.

rows.description: When the introduced perfecto use fits (O7).
sourceCells: Use sufficient familiar time/situation context, including taught adverbs where useful. Separate a named-tense formation task from an unlabelled meaning choice; do not require untaught past forms.

rows.description: A short account or message: understand and write (O8/O9).
sourceCells: Read a brief prepared text and give a relevant written account/answer with familiar words and introduced meanings.

rows.description: Optional mixed check and delayed independent return.
sourceCells: Sample auxiliary, regular/irregular participles, accents, sentence structure, and meaning in short resumable tasks. Preserve specific evidence; comparison with other past tenses follows their introduction.

rows.description: Produce introduced regular -ar indefinido forms for the intended person.
sourceCells: S1 9.1.3 regular-paradigm anchor; exact lexical/person allocation and written accents require review.

rows.description: Produce introduced regular -er/-ir indefinido forms.
sourceCells: S1 9.1.3 and S7 tables. Reuse person awareness without assuming present endings transfer unchanged.

rows.description: Preserve introduced spelling/diacritic patterns in an appropriate past form.
sourceCells: S1's orthography cross-references and S7 models are provisional anchors. Review selected spelling-preserving patterns and their person restrictions; do not label every spelling issue a tense-choice failure.

rows.description: Produce selected person-specific vowel changes in introduced -ir verbs.
sourceCells: S7 model 46 shows pedir forms including pidió/pidieron. Teach the relevant persons and exact selected verb family; do not apply a present-stem rule to every past form.

rows.description: Produce selected forms with the introduced y alternation.
sourceCells: S7 model 40 shows leer forms including leyó/leyeron. Keep this pattern distinguishable from O4 and review the final lexical set.

rows.description: Recall selected common irregular stems/forms, including needed small exceptional paradigms.
sourceCells: S1 9.1.3 identifies tener/hacer/estar and ver/dar; S7 provides form tables. Exact additional verbs, endings, and exceptional persons remain review work.

rows.description: Form and interpret introduced ser/ir past uses with enough context to identify the meaning.
sourceCells: S1 9.1.3 and S7 models. Shared surface forms do not identify the lexical meaning alone; ambiguous prompts need clarification or reviewed alternatives.

rows.description: Choose an introduced indefinido meaning in a sufficiently bounded past-event context.
sourceCells: S1 9.1.3 supplies the basic event/time anchor. Introduce a limited reviewed contrast with known perfecto; avoid a keyword-only rule or an untaught imperfecto choice.

rows.description: Extract the sequence/meaning of a short familiar past account.
sourceCells: Reading and listening evidence remain distinguishable from recalling forms in writing. Teach time links and supporting vocabulary first.

rows.description: Write a short relevant sequence of completed events or a practical reply.
sourceCells: Use introduced patterns, suitable time context, and reviewed valid variants rather than requiring a reference text verbatim.

rows.description: Regular -ar past forms (O1).
sourceCells: Link person and ending, complete a familiar form, then write a short event sentence with meaningful time context.

rows.description: Regular -er/-ir past forms (O2).
sourceCells: Practice the taught pattern, change person, and produce familiar action statements. Keep relevant accents visible in explanation and independently assessed later.

rows.description: Selected spelling changes and written accents (O3).
sourceCells: Explain each introduced pattern/person restriction, correct a supported form, and later recall it in a different familiar context.

rows.description: Selected vowel changes and y forms in small separate steps (O4/O5).
sourceCells: Use a small reviewed set such as pedir/leer, compare the relevant persons, and retain separate pattern evidence before mixing tasks.

rows.description: Frequent irregular stems and other selected forms (O6).
sourceCells: Introduce a manageable set, group useful patterns, and practice individual difficult forms. The exact list is pending; do not demand every irregular verb at once.

rows.description: Ser and ir: form plus contextual meaning (O7).
sourceCells: Form the introduced paradigm and understand which meaning fits the authored situation. A named-verb gap is different evidence from independent interpretation.

rows.description: When the event is framed as completed (O8).
sourceCells: Choose an appropriate introduced tense with sufficient context, then begin reviewed contrasts with known perfecto. Later past contrasts follow A2-05/A2-06.

rows.description: Put past events in sequence (O9/O10).
sourceCells: Read a short prepared account and write a few relevant linked events or a reply using familiar words and introduced time links. Receive already taught sequence links (CV-04).

rows.description: Optional mixed check and delayed independent return.
sourceCells: Sample regular patterns, spelling, selected exceptions, lexical meaning, and contextual use in short resumable tasks. Preserve granular evidence rather than a whole-tense mastery label.

rows.description: Produce introduced regular -ar imperfecto forms for the intended person.
sourceCells: S1 9.1.2 regular-paradigm anchor and S7 models; teach the -aba pattern in manageable person steps. Make reference/person clear where surface forms coincide.

rows.description: Produce introduced regular -er/-ir imperfecto forms.
sourceCells: S1 9.1.2 and S7; teach the -ía pattern explicitly rather than carrying over present/indefinido endings. Exact lexical/person allocation requires review.

rows.description: Recall the introduced ser, ir, and ver imperfecto forms.
sourceCells: S1 9.1.2 identifies these exceptions; S7 models 61/38/68 provide forms. Preserve individual form/person targets for later review.

rows.description: Preserve relevant written accents in introduced imperfecto forms.
sourceCells: S7 tables, including éramos and veíamos; review the exact regular/exception patterns. A spelling correction is not automatically a contextual-tense error.

rows.description: Express an introduced past habit/routine in sufficient context.
sourceCells: S1 9.1.2 habitual/cyclical-use anchor. Teach any frequency/time expression first; a marker alone is not a universal tense selector.

rows.description: Describe a familiar past person, object, place, or setting using introduced frames.
sourceCells: S1 9.1.2 descriptive-use anchor, including time/setting. Teach any needed age, weather, or impersonal frame before assessing it; no untaught compound past is assumed.

rows.description: Describe an introduced past situation/activity as background and begin a reviewed viewpoint contrast with known indefinido.
sourceCells: This is a local teaching proposal needing full source/context review. Supply enough meaning context and permitted readings; do not reduce the distinction to long/short or unfinished/finished action labels.

rows.description: Extract the relevant meaning of a short past routine/description.
sourceCells: Keep reading/listening comprehension distinguishable from writing a verb form. Any needed linking expression is introduced first.

rows.description: Write a brief relevant past routine, memory, or description.
sourceCells: Use familiar introduced material and reviewed valid variants. A reference text is a model, not the sole accepted wording.

rows.description: Regular -ar forms with the -aba pattern (O1/O4).
sourceCells: Connect person and ending, complete/correct a familiar form, then write a short supported past statement. Attribute accent support separately.

rows.description: Regular -er/-ir forms with the -ía pattern (O2/O4).
sourceCells: Practice the introduced person forms and relevant accents before mixing them with prior present/past endings.

rows.description: Ser, ir, and ver exceptions (O3/O4).
sourceCells: Introduce the reviewed forms in small steps and revisit individual difficult person/form pairs in varied familiar contexts.

rows.description: Past habits and routines (O5).
sourceCells: Understand a familiar routine, choose a suitable introduced meaning, and write a short statement with taught time/frequency expressions.

rows.description: Describe a past person, place, or situation (O6).
sourceCells: Reuse familiar description/agreement; explicitly introduce needed past age/time/weather/state frames before independent work. Receive the present-to-past age/weather handoff (CV-04).

rows.description: A past situation as background: initial meaning contrast (O7).
sourceCells: Use a short authored situation to compare introduced imperfecto/indefinido readings. Review natural alternatives and teach any needed link; full mixed practice follows in A2-06.

rows.description: A short memory or past routine (O8/O9).
sourceCells: Read a brief prepared account and write a few relevant descriptive/routine statements or an appropriate reply.

rows.description: Optional mixed check and delayed independent return.
sourceCells: Sample regular patterns, individual exceptions, accents, and introduced meanings in short resumable tasks. Preserve specific evidence instead of a whole-tense mastery label.

rows.description: Distinguish an introduced present situation/routine from a past one in a sufficiently framed familiar context.
sourceCells: Reuse A1-03/04 and A2-01/03/04/05. Start with controlled contrasts rather than all four forms at once.

rows.description: Choose between introduced perfecto compuesto and indefinido readings.
sourceCells: Reuse A2-03/A2-04 and recorded S1 9.1.6/9.1.3 anchors. Exact Spain contexts and permitted alternatives still require review; a time word alone must not determine a unique key.

rows.description: Choose between introduced indefinido and imperfecto readings.
sourceCells: Reuse A2-04/A2-05 and recorded S1 9.1.3/9.1.2 anchors. Review event/background/habit viewpoint and natural alternatives rather than using action duration as a universal rule.

rows.description: Produce the needed introduced form after its intended meaning/construction is clear.
sourceCells: Link evidence back to existing family/person, auxiliary, participle, individual exception, and orthography targets. An explicitly supplied tense supports form evidence, not independent tense-choice evidence.

rows.description: Select suitable introduced constructions in a short mixed situation without tense labels.
sourceCells: Combine only taught meanings and frames; give sufficient temporal/reference context. Multiple valid readings need reviewed alternatives or the unresolved path.

rows.description: Extract the relevant time relationship or situation meaning from a short text or recording.
sourceCells: Reuse written/listening boundaries. Answering a meaning question does not by itself demonstrate independent conjugation or written production.

rows.description: Write a brief connected account or reply using suitable familiar present/past constructions.
sourceCells: Use reviewed variants, short resumable tasks, and clear communicative intent. Do not require a particular tense count or exact reference-text wording.

rows.description: Now and before: introduced present versus past meanings (O1).
sourceCells: Compare short familiar situations, choose an appropriate statement, then write a relevant sentence. Begin with one contrast at a time.

rows.description: Perfecto compuesto or indefinido in context (O2).
sourceCells: Read the intended situation, compare reviewed alternatives, and complete/write a short statement. Keep contextual choice separate from haber/participle or indefinido recall.

rows.description: Indefinido or imperfecto in context (O3).
sourceCells: Work with introduced events, habits, descriptions, and background in short authored situations. Supply enough information to support the intended reading and review valid alternatives.

rows.description: Untangle similar or forgotten forms (O4).
sourceCells: With meaning/construction supplied, compare and recall familiar person/form pairs. Use relevant recorded difficulties, or a neutral sample when evidence is absent; preserve individual exceptions such as hecho and the introduced ser/ir/ver targets.

rows.description: Mixed everyday situations without tense labels (O5).
sourceCells: Move from paired contrasts to a small mixed set using familiar topics. Select/write a fitting sentence; optional Ukrainian reasoning can support reflection but is not a required terminology exam.

rows.description: A short account or practical reply (O6/O7).
sourceCells: Read or listen for meaning, then write a few relevant statements or a reply. Separate comprehension and production steps so one answer is not treated as proof of every skill.

rows.description: Optional mixed check and delayed independent return.
sourceCells: Sample introduced contrasts and specific forms in short resumable tasks without a visible tense/model cue. Keep help available and retain its actual scope. No compulsory perfect score or whole-tense mastery label.

rows.description: Write a short request for an object, action, or help appropriate to a stated situation.
sourceCells: S6 4.1-4.4 provides partial request anchors. Introduce the chosen present/infinitive patterns and politeness expressions; context must identify who is asking whom.

rows.description: Ask permission and give a suitable brief acceptance or refusal with a reason where needed.
sourceCells: S6 4.7-4.10. Distinguish the requested action, speaker/addressee, response meaning, and verb form. Exact registers and variants require review.

rows.description: Produce introduced regular affirmative instructions to one or several familiar addressees.
sourceCells: S1 9.3 regular singular/plural second-person anchor; teach tú/vosotros forms in manageable steps for the Spain target.

rows.description: Recall selected frequent irregular affirmative instruction forms.
sourceCells: S1 9.3 lists examples di/haz/pon/sal. Exact vocabulary/person sets need review; each difficult form retains its own evidence.

rows.description: Use introduced affirmative usted/ustedes forms when the stated situation calls for them.
sourceCells: S1 9.3 treatment-form anchor. Teach the selected forms explicitly; do not assume prior productive subjunctive knowledge or infer politeness from one ending alone.

rows.description: Attach a taught object pronoun to an introduced affirmative imperative with appropriate written accents.
sourceCells: S1 9.3, with its pronoun/orthography cross-references. Begin with supported simple attachments; exact accent patterns and any multi-pronoun expansion require separate mapping/review.

rows.description: Extract the action, addressee, and order of steps in a short practical instruction or recording.
sourceCells: S6 4.1 and the written/listening course outcomes. Reuse introduced affirmative/obligation patterns and teach sequence links before assessment.

rows.description: Write a brief practical message containing a clear request/instruction or reply, with relevant details and a reason.
sourceCells: Original synthesis of introduced functions and prior text skills. Judge communicative fit separately from form, reference, and orthography; a model is not the sole valid wording.

rows.description: Request an object, action, or help (O1).
sourceCells: Compare short situated requests, complete a familiar pattern, and write a request. Teach the selected polite expressions and pronoun roles first.

rows.description: Permission and a short response (O2).
sourceCells: Distinguish asking to act from asking someone else to act; write an acceptance or a refusal with a familiar reason.

rows.description: Regular affirmative instructions: tú/vosotros (O3).
sourceCells: Introduce person/number contrasts in small steps, then complete or write a familiar instruction. Keep addressee recognition separate from form recall.

rows.description: Frequent irregular instruction forms (O4).
sourceCells: Practice selected exceptions in familiar contexts and return to specific difficult forms rather than labeling the entire imperative weak.

rows.description: Affirmative instructions with usted/ustedes (O5).
sourceCells: Introduce the needed forms and address context explicitly; compare reviewed alternatives without treating every public situation as requiring one register.

rows.description: A pronoun joined to an instruction (O6).
sourceCells: Identify the intended object, attach a taught pronoun, and check the resulting written form. Separate role, placement, and accent evidence.

rows.description: Understand short instructions and their order (O7).
sourceCells: Read a brief note or listen to prepared directions; identify needed actions/steps using familiar vocabulary and introduced links. Meaning questions do not require an unrelated conjugation. Teach selected impersonal obligation and fixed-notice meaning before later reading (CV-05/CV-06).

rows.description: A useful short message with a reason (O8).
sourceCells: Write a request, instruction, or response about home, a purchase, an appointment, or a simple problem. Give enough recipient/purpose context and permit reviewed variants. Reuse introduced impersonal obligation where appropriate (CV-05).

rows.description: Optional mixed check and delayed independent return.
sourceCells: Sample request/response meaning, specific forms, pronoun attachment, and practical text comprehension/production in short resumable tasks. Help remains available; no mandatory perfect score.

rows.description: Extract relevant facts or required actions from a short practical text.
sourceCells: Reuse A1-05/A2-07 and the recorded S2 text direction. Distinguish understanding dates, quantities, places, and instructions from spelling a Spanish response.

rows.description: Identify the purpose, participants, and relevant details of a short message.
sourceCells: Reuse A1-06/A2-02/A2-07. Review reference and communicative context; do not require unrelated verb production to demonstrate comprehension.

rows.description: Understand an introduced past account and write a brief relevant continuation or reply.
sourceCells: Reuse A2-03 through A2-06; retain separate time/viewpoint meaning, specific form, and writing evidence. No new past construction is presumed.

rows.description: Compare familiar options and explain a suitable choice in a short written response.
sourceCells: Reuse A2-02, preferences, reasons, and practical details. Review multiple sensible responses; there is no arbitrary single correct personal preference.

rows.description: Understand the main point and selected details of a short prepared Spain recording.
sourceCells: Reuse C-054 listening boundaries. Separate audio-only meaning, transcript/replay-supported work, dictation, and any subsequent written response.

rows.description: Write a short connected message suited to the stated recipient and purpose.
sourceCells: Reuse introduced sentence links, reference, requests, descriptions, and time forms as needed; assess relevance and clarity separately from individual language errors.

rows.description: Reuse a reviewed personal construction in a suitable familiar situation.
sourceCells: C-022/C-023: exact recall and suitable variation use distinct evidence. Only reviewed entries become answer models; missing personal material can use a prepared course alternative.

rows.description: Review and revise a short draft using appropriate feedback or reference help.
sourceCells: Original support objective. Keep first-attempt and supported revision evidence distinct; a corrected draft does not itself prove later independent recall.

rows.description: A notice or practical information (O1).
sourceCells: Read a short opening-hours notice, appointment note, or instruction; find needed details and answer a relevant short question. Use adopted notice/form/menu/schedule contexts only after their needed frames are taught (CV-05/CV-06).

rows.description: Read a message and respond (O2/O6).
sourceCells: Identify the request, participants, and missing information; write a suitable brief response using familiar language.

rows.description: A short account of the past (O3).
sourceCells: Read a familiar event/routine description and write a few relevant statements or a reply. Retain the original form/exception and contrast targets.

rows.description: Compare options and explain a choice (O4/O6).
sourceCells: Compare two familiar plans, products, places, or schedules, then give a brief reason. Provide enough information and permit reviewed alternatives.

rows.description: Understand a short recording (O5).
sourceCells: Begin with an audio-only meaning question, offer help on request, and optionally follow with a written reply as a separate task.

rows.description: A useful text with personal constructions (O6/O7/O8).
sourceCells: Write a short message using suitable reviewed phrases or a prepared alternative; reread and revise with available feedback. Personal content stays private.

rows.description: Optional cumulative check in short parts and a delayed return.
sourceCells: Sample reading, listening, and writing across familiar situations with pause/resume. Keep parts and evidence separate; no mandatory long exam, perfect score, or topic lock.
